draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Matheran! Its name means 'forest on the forehead' of the mountains, and it's one of India's smallest hill stations, where cars aren't allowed in.
draft.hungryLine: I don't have a named place to eat in my notes for Matheran, so ask at your hotel or one of the old bungalows about what's good today.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Madhavji Point is just a 7 minute walk, Khandala Point about 12, and Echo Point around 17 minutes away.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Walk the red laterite paths out to Maria Point or Honeymoon Point, both about 15 minutes away, and enjoy the quiet.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Matheran is so close to the city it's part of the Mumbai Metropolitan Region, about 90 km from Mumbai.

tips.title: Leave the car behind.
tips.body: No automobiles are allowed in Matheran, so walk, ride a horse, or take the Aman Lodge shuttle train from the parking area.

tips.title: The shuttle runs in the monsoon.
tips.body: The Aman Lodge to Matheran service keeps going through the rains, saving you the 3 km walk.

story.title: Forest on the forehead
story.body: Matheran sits at about 800 m in the Western Ghats. Its Marathi name means the forest on the forehead of the mountains.

story.title: Bungalows on red earth
story.body: Hotels and Parsi bungalows came up along roads of red laterite earth. The town still keeps its British colonial architecture.

story.title: The Hill Railway
story.body: The narrow gauge Matheran Hill Railway climbs up from Neral. Matheran station is its fifth and last stop.

story.title: An eco-sensitive escape
story.body: The Ministry of Environment has declared Matheran an eco-sensitive region. It's a favourite weekend getaway from Mumbai and Pune.
